18.description: The committee recommends a new transit bylaw to enhance safety, allowing bans and $50 fines for specific offenses. It will also maintain current rules for pets (service animals or kennelled).

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Pears questioned the proposed $50 fine for transit offenses.
Families with children under six, potentially facing hardship from supervision rules.
Administration changed pet policy to reduce operator conflict; committee reverted it.
How a small enforcement team will assure compliance across 90 buses.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon supported bylaw intent but opposed relaxing pet rules.
Sporadic enforcement could lead to charges of harassment and discrimination.
Child supervision rules could cause undue hardship for some families.
Administration will provide leisure center child supervision policy for comparison.

19.description: Saskatoon Transit is implementing a multi-pronged strategy to address rising fare evasion, including a new bylaw allowing officers to issue tickets and a transit policing program. This aims to improve compliance and safety.

chips.text: Approved
6 for, 0 against
Councillor Pearce questioned the accuracy of the 1.8% fare evasion rate
High school students and unhoused individuals are identified as key groups of fare evaders.
Administration confirmed the 1.8% fare evasion rate is likely an underestimate
Bus Riders of Saskatoon highlighted Saskatoon's $66 low-income pass versus Calgary's $6.
Council will receive a one-year progress report on police transit support.

20.description: Saskatoon Transit is redesigning its bus network, seeking public input on prioritizing ridership or coverage. This update outlines future engagement phases.

chips.text: Councillor questioned survey wording on bus stop distance, seeking clearer parameters.
Future bus network changes will affect shift workers, students, and those with mobility challenges.
Exact amount spent from the $100,000 engagement budget was not immediately provided.
Bus Riders of Saskatoon advocated for more hands-on, in-depth public engagement sessions.
The bus network redesign engagement has an estimated budget of $100,000 over three years.

21.description: Saskatoon Transit's 2025 annual report details a 6.7% ridership decrease, ongoing fleet renewal, and progress on rapid transit lines. It also outlines service expansions and safety initiatives.

chips.text: City Manager explained Saskatchewan's unique untethered provincial revenue sharing model.
Residents in Brighton, Rosewood, and Aspen Ridge received expanded transit service.
Specific data on international student impact on ridership was unavailable.
Access Transit improved booking and reduced trip denial rates to 9%.
Staff will communicate upcoming summer and fall route adjustments to riders.

22.description: Saskatoon's Standing Policy Committee on Transportation reviewed its list of ongoing referrals, a semi-annual update on items previously sent for further action.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Updated referral lists will be provided to the committee every six months
